transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Salieri! I’ve been away for two weeks on the Emperor’s business, trusting you to keep the rehearsals on schedule! The singers don’t know their entrances, the second violin parts are missing entirely, and someone has rewritten my stage directions without a word to me! The premiere is in ten days! You gave me your word that everything would be in order!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Ah, my dear colleague, it is indeed regrettable to hear of the state of disarray in which you have found our preparations. I must offer my sincerest apologies for the shortcomings that have occurred in your absence. Rest assured, I had every intention of upholding my promise to keep the rehearsals on track.

It seems there has been a grave misunderstanding or miscommunication that has led to this unfortunate situation. Let us work together to rectify these errors swiftly and diligently. I shall personally ensure that the missing violin parts are copied without delay, and I will see to it that the singers receive the necessary guidance to master their entrances.

As for the altered stage directions, it is indeed perplexing that such changes were made without your consultation. Please accept my assurances that I had no knowledge of this alteration, and I share your concern regarding the integrity of the production. Let us review the revised directions together and, if necessary, restore them to their original form in accordance with your vision.

With ten days remaining until the premiere, time is of the essence. Let us put our differences aside and focus on the task at hand, for the sake of the opera and the Emperor's expectations. I am committed to working in harmony with you to ensure that our performance shines brightly on the grand stage.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Misunderstanding? Miscommunication, Salieri? I left you a detailed schedule, annotated scores, and the complete stage plans! How can a *misunderstanding* result in missing violin parts and singers who sound like they’re sight-reading for the first time? And the stage directions – my cues for lighting, for scene changes, the very *flow* of the drama – completely rewritten! Someone has actively interfered, and it happened on *your* watch!

"Without delay," you say, for the violin parts? Do you know how long it takes a good scribe to copy forty pages of music, let alone forty *missing* pages, perfectly, for an entire section of the orchestra? We've lost two weeks of rehearsal time, actual practice, because these fundamental elements weren't even *present*!

And to "review" the revised directions? My directions were meticulous! Who *dared* to change them? Who has the authority, other than the composer, to alter the very fabric of the opera? This isn't a mere oversight, Antonio, this is a sabotage of the production! We have ten days! Ten! How are we supposed to fix *all* of this in ten days when we should be perfecting, not scrambling to put the pieces back together? My word, I feel like I've walked into a nightmare!

We have *ten days*! That's barely enough time to polish, not to rebuild from the foundation!

Are you telling me you had no knowledge of *any* of this happening? Not a whisper, not a hint, that such monumental changes were being made under your nose? I find that incredibly difficult to believe, Salieri. You were in charge!
